_note: The view of the mountains (2026-11-15, branch arashiyama-vista; VistaRules, VistaMountain, Main3D). The play camera looks 16 degrees down at the top of the frame, so no mountain ever shows from it: a few viewpoints tilt the camera up while the farmer stands in them and ease it back as he leaves. They keep the play camera's yaw (45, looking north-west), so the move keys still match the screen (a first try turned the camera round to the south and the user found it dizzying and hard to steer); the mountains to see stand where it looks. `mountains`: the land rising past the maps, in plan cells (data/world.json, the village at [0, 0]), built on the maps in `maps` (each in its own cells, moved by its place on the plan). Each is a `ridge` of [x, z, height] points (world units, a cell is 1): the ground at a point is the ridge's height at the nearest point of the line less `slope` x the distance to it, with `lumps` (a value noise `lump_scale` cells across) on top, and it eases down to nothing within `foot` cells of any map on the plan and of the water running off the maps (`foot` [start, full]: from past the land beyond a map's edges, 14 cells, so the play camera sees no slope close by; the water carried `corridor` cells, or out to where two streams meet: the river runs out of the gorge in a valley), so it never stands on a cell anyone walks; `far_water` cells from a map's edge the water running off it is carried on past the apron, straight on (2026-11-20: past the apron the open land left a hole over the river, and its grass sloped down into it like a chasm, the user's word): only down the plan's corridors (VistaRules.far_river), laid cell by cell as the apron lays the map's own: its bed at the water's depth, stone walls, two cells of grass either side at the land's height, the moving skin over it, a stone wall across its far end (VistaMountain._add_river, Surroundings); Ogura's and Arashiyama's `area` run west to -220 (2026-11-20) so the open land runs on past the river's far end and no sky shows under the far hills down the gorge; `apron_runs_as` what a map's edge ground runs on as past the edge (the bamboo hill's cliff and scree would run on as fourteen cells of bare stone: grass, its pines and snow); `apron_pines` the pines in a hundred cells of the land past these maps' edges (thinner than the 45 elsewhere); `apron_trees` per map: there the wood past the edges is `share` trees in a hundred cells, of which `kinds` (kind -> %) are broadleaf (Nishiki Hill: cherries, maples and ginkgos on the slopes round it, seen in their season, no pines: its kinds add to 100) and the rest pines; `foot_blend` units over which a slope's foot takes the open grass's colour (the grass picture's average times the season's `foot`) before the forest's; `sink` keeps its foot below the land past the edges. `area` [x0, z0, x1, z1] bounds the mesh, `step` cells between its points. Kitayama: the far hills north beyond the bamboo hill, filling the hill's view to the north. Ogura: north-west of the village, beyond the farm and west of Kaminoda and the bamboo hill, as on the real map: the one the viewpoints look at. Arashiyama: south and south-west across the river from the long bridge, wrapping round the gorge's mouth to the west and on behind Minamino (Iwatayama); only its foot shows from the play camera, past the south-west edges. A ridge ends low and the mesh's `area` runs on past it, so it never stops in a cliff. `colors` by season: `foot` the colour the open land's grass is multiplied by at the mountains' feet, darkening over 12 cells toward them (none under snow), `dark` and `light` the forest's two tones, `accent` the patches among them on `accent_share` (0..1) of the slope (spring's and fall's shares 0 since 2026-11-20: spring's pale pink patches read as grey stains and fall's red-orange ones as orange stains on the slope, the user's word; the fall wood keeps its olive and brown tones), `snow` on what lies above `snow_line` (a share of the highest peak, 1 for none): a soft line, lying thick on the gentle slopes and thin on the steep ones, dark trees showing through it near the line, lit by the sun and blue-grey in shade (2026-11-20: a flat 85% white over the forest's light read as fog, not snow). `ambient` the share of light in shade; `haze` [near, far, most]: the sky's colour laid over it by its distance from the eye. `views`: on map `map`, the cells `rect` [x, y, w, h]: the camera keeps `yaw` (degrees; the play camera's 45, the eye south-east of the farmer; another would turn it the short way round), looks down `pitch` (degrees, less than the play camera's 30), through `fov` (vertical degrees), `dist` units back from the target, which sits `lift` units over the farmer's feet; it eases in and out over `ease` seconds. More viewpoints (2026-11-19): `gorge` the whole river map (the gorge upstream: Ogura over the far bank's pines), `farm_pond` the farm pond's west and north banks and the fishing spot (x 24-28, y 1-4: Ogura over the pond, looking level (pitch 0): Ogura stands nearest the farm, so at the bridge's pitch 8 its ridge ran past the top of the frame and the slope filled the sky like a wall; clear of the gate road (31, 5..6), the barn's yard (y 5..6) and the silo's cells and the cells in front of it (x 29-30)), `minamino_bank` Minamino's riverside at the lane's end (rows 16-19: clear of the path round Kiku's front, row 15). Sakurazaka's bridge was scouted and left out: its roofed bridge fills the tilted view. A view with `soak` true is only there while the farmer sits in a bath (VistaRules.view_at's `soaking`): `kajika_soak` (2026-11-24, the user's photo of a forest onsen) brings the camera down and in over Kajika-yu's pool while they soak, easing back as they get out; the gorge has a broadleaf wood past its edges (`apron_trees` kajika: maples and cherries). Balance numbers are ours.
